articles.title: Recantations can aid Martin, say House allies
articles.summary: Recantations of several witnesses in the flood control controversy could help weaken the plunder case against Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez, two of his allies said yesterday.

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

Contributed photo shows a team led by PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez serving the arrest warrant on former speaker Martin Romualdez, who has a detainee’s shirt draped over his hospital clothing, at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center last night. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla also went to the hospital.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Recantations of several witnesses in the flood control controversy could help weaken the plunder case against Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez, two of his allies said yesterday.
Former congressman Robert Ace Barbers and Rep. Joel Chua said witnesses’ retraction of their testimonies implicating the former House speaker could serve as a mitigating factor in his case.
“Four or five of (18 men) have made their recantations. And this, I think, will have an impact when it reaches trial,” Barbers said. “What that impact will be, I still have no idea.”
“We respect the ombudsman’s findings and we expect that the former speaker will exhaust all the remedies to protect his right,” Chua said.
President Marcos did not intervene in the arrest of his cousin Romualdez, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said yesterday.

“Martin and I are also close, but in the interest of the State, we will do everything,” Remulla said, noting that he and his brother Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla belong to the same fraternity as Romualdez. – Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Defense, prosecution can grill Sara’s security officers
articles.summary: In a reversal of his previous ruling, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said he will now allow both the defense and the prosecution to direct and cross-examine Vice…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

'Scam ito': Kapunan says on alleged OVP fund misuse at impeachment trial Defense counsel Michael Poa (left) and prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan examine witness Roderick Wamil during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Aug. 4, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit

MANILA, Philippines — In a reversal of his previous ruling, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said he will now allow both the defense and the prosecution to direct and cross-examine Vice President Sara Duterte’s security officers, Colonels Dennis Nolasco and Raymund Dante Lachica, in case they are summoned to the witness stand.

“Several senator-judges have already inquired if we can call Cols. Lachica and Nolasco, and at the proper time, the court said yesterday, the presiding officer said yesterday that we may consider doing that after the defense shall have rested on this article or after the proceedings before we arrive at a decision. We will afford the parties due process by giving both parties, since these are witnesses called by the court itself, we will afford both parties to cross-examine the witness should the court decide to call them,” Escudero said yesterday.

Senator-judges have been prodding the prosecution to present Lachica and Nolasco after they were tagged by special disbursing officer Gina Acosta and Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio as the ones who distributed the secret funds to informants of both the OVP and the Department of Education when Duterte was secretary.
VP as witness?

Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel said it intends to call Duterte to the witness stand in her own impeachment trial as it rested its presentation of evidence on alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article 1 of the Articles of Impeachment yesterday.

Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said the prosecution would no longer present its remaining 15 witnesses, which she dubbed as “pawns, bishops, castles and horses” in a game of chess, for Article 1, which alleges that the Vice President misused or misappropriated P612.5-million worth of confidential funds.

Kapunan explained that the prosecution’s decision to forgo the remaining witnesses was because the case “has become very clear” and that the testimony so far “elicited very clearly a pattern as one would see a chessboard.”

“All of these pawns and castles and horses and bishops point to only one person, and that accountable person is the Vice President. That’s why, in lieu of presenting 15 other witnesses, we will be presenting the Vice President herself as regards misuse and misappropriation of confidential funds,” Kapunan said. – Daphne Galvez, Bella Cariaso, Delon Porcalla, Ghio Ong

articles.title: VP will attend arraignment on Friday – Poa
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte will be physically present at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday in connection with the three counts of grave threats filed by the Department of Justice…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte shows a document after posting bail at a court building in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte will be physically present at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday in connection with the three counts of grave threats filed by the Department of Justice (DOJ) against her.
At a press conference yesterday, defense spokesman Michael Poa said Duterte’s physical attendance is required during her arraignment.
“At the arraignment, the accused must be there to enter a plea or not to enter a plea if she so decides,” he said.
On Saturday, Duterte posted P360,000 bail for three counts of grave threats directed at President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez.
Poa accompanied Duterte when she posted bail before the Quezon City RTC Branch 98.

At the same time, Poa was mum after Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Duterte’s camp initially wanted her to be arrested and jailed at Camp Crame, asking about detention arrangements, including food, before deciding to proceed to the court to post bail.
“I cannot comment on that,” Poa added.
Remulla said Duterte’s team apparently wanted to generate images of the Vice President behind bars and in handcuffs.
Poa said he has yet to discuss with Duterte if he will accompany her during her arraignment. – Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: All NLEX San Simon lanes reopen
articles.summary: The North Luzon Expressway is now fully open to vehicular traffic with the completion by the Department of Public Works and Highways of initial structural works to prevent monsoon-induced heavy…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am
Motorists pile up in heavy traffic as some passengers walk along the NLEX to get to a nearby gas station at San Simon in Pampanga on Aug. 31, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) is now fully open to vehicular traffic with the completion by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) of initial structural works to prevent monsoon-induced heavy flooding, the latest of which lasted for days and left traffic at a standstill, especially along the San Simon and Tulaoc Bridge sections.

Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon said emergency engineering task forces, working together with NLEX Corp. and San Miguel Corp. (SMC), completed the installation of reinforced steel sheet piles along vulnerable embankment gaps to prevent river overflows from spilling onto the tollway.

“Phase 1 is now complete. With sheet pile containment structures firmly in place, we are confident that this critical trade segment is protected even if river levels rise or high tides hit Manila Bay in the coming weeks,” Dizon told reporters during an inspection of the area yesterday.

In Pampanga, at least 7,343 families or 26,322 people remain in evacuation centers as flooding continues to affect communities across the province, according to the latest report of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO).

The figure was recorded in 415 evacuation centers across the province. Santo Tomas town recorded 1,112 families or 3,951 people staying in seven evacuation centers. Bacolor has 663 families or 2,516 people in 15 centers.
The local government of Guagua reported 382 families or 1,334 people in 43 evacuation centers.
Outside the evacuation centers, 329 families or 1,122 people in Guagua and 24 families or 112 people in Porac are staying in safe places.
The provincial government said it has been providing potable water, managing evacuation centers, deploying water purifiers and distributing food packs to affected communities.
The PDRRMO report covers the combined effects of Tropical Depressions Luis, Maymay and Neneng, Tropical Storm Pilandok and the southwest monsoon.
Damage to agriculture due to the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones last month has breached P4 billion, according to the Department of Agriculture.
Based on the final bulletin of the DA, the damage to agriculture including fisheries was at P4.38 billion.
This affected 99,663 farmers and fisherfolk, covering 81,511 hectares of agricultural areas and 102,791 metric tons of production losses. – Ric Sapnu, Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Chinese fighter jets intercept Philippine patrol aircraft
articles.summary: In yet another display of “coercive and aggressive actions,” Chinese fighter jets intercepted a Philippine aircraft patrolling Panatag (Scarborough) Shoal or Bajo de Masinloc last week,…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — In yet another display of “coercive and aggressive actions,” Chinese fighter jets intercepted a Philippine aircraft patrolling Panatag (Scarborough) Shoal or Bajo de Masinloc last week, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) confirmed yesterday.
The AFP said the action by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force aims to weaken the Philippines’ resolve in patrolling and protecting its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

AFP spokesman for the West Philippine Sea, retired rear admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, said a J-10 trainer aircraft intercepted a Philippine maritime domain awareness (MDA) flight over Panatag Shoal on Sept. 2.

“Regular maritime air patrol domain awareness flights were conducted over Bajo de Masinloc. They were intercepted by fighter aircraft from the PLA Air Force or the PLA Navy,” he told reporters at a press briefing yesterday.

“In one instance, the crosshairs (gunsights) of the fighter aircraft had our aircraft on it and this was released in the South China Morning Post and the Global Times addressing the internal audience,” he noted.

“These are coercive and aggressive actions designed to show that they have control over the situation over the area. It is designed to weaken our resolve to keep performing our mandate. It is designed to show that they have escalation dynamics on their side,” Trinidad added.
Despite such actions by China, he said the Philippines will not back down and will continue to patrol and assert its sovereign rights over the WPS.

“Rather than weaken our resolve, such actions will only further strengthen it. Our resolve to keep performing our mandate has never been stronger. They have not even succeeded in preventing us from performing our patrols,” he said.

“Not only will we keep performing our mandate, we will keep working with our treaty ally and other like-minded nations who have been very supportive of our stand of supporting international law, especially Japan and Australia,” Trinidad declared.
As to what actions or adjustments the AFP will take, he explained that details on how MDA flights are conducted are left to the commanders of the military’s unified commands.
Gibo slams China

Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. lashed out at China yesterday after he was handed a note stating the former’s position on the WPS issue while he was answering questions at the 2026 Seoul Defense Dialogue (SDD) in South Korea.
“Please show some decency. Shame on you,” said Teodoro, who drew applause for answering China’s note point by point during the international forum.
“I think this is from China,” Teodoro read the note and answered each of China’s arguments, saying the move showed “disrespect” of the defense dialogue and the host country.

“China’s position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent and firm. They have no position. The arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law. So, what you signed, UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea), you mean violates international law. That’s what you mean,” he said.
“The so-called award is illegal, null and void. So say you. And has no binding force. Because you don’t want to be subjected to UNCLOS,” he continued.
“China neither accepts nor recognizes the award. Of course, because you lost. And oppose it and we’ll never accept any claim or action arising from it,” Teodoro finished.

“These are words that (were) slipped to me. And there is a legal principle called res ipsa loquitur – the thing speaks for itself. How can you deal with a country in an international forum beyond the question asked to me,” he noted, referring to how he was seemingly ambushed by the note.

In his plenary remarks at the two-day event attended by international defense leaders from across regions, Teodoro talked about how the main purpose that the United Nations was created several years ago to a world war has “succeeded in that sense.”

Without specifically mentioning any country, he said the threat of conflict and actual conflict remains “but the threat of war becomes more imminent because of unconstrained and uncontrolled use of might versus right, as the adage goes.”

Teodoro said the Philippines will likewise “advocate for an international security architecture which has for its fundamental value human security, the survival of the human being, care for the human being, care for human rights, care for health, care for freedom from dangers of natural calamities, educational opportunities for mutual understanding under a regime of freedom of thought, freedom of speech and not state-sponsored lies and state-sponsored brainwashing.”

Teodoro underscored the need to build an international security architecture with human security at its core as he discussed the Philippines’ perspective on building a “Collaborative Architecture for International Stability.”

Joined by South Korean Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back and Czech Republic Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence Jaromír Z?na, he echoed their observations on “the whole gamut of conflicts facing the world at present, which is exacerbated by the existence of devastating natural calamities.”
Marcos Jr. : Promote awareness
President Marcos called on Filipinos to promote awareness on the Philippines’ rights and entitlements to its waters as the nation observes the Maritime and Archipelagic Nation Awareness Month.
September has been declared Maritime and Archipelagic Nation Awareness Month through Proclamation 316 issued in 2017.

Marcos said this year’s observance, held alongside the 10th anniversary of the 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award, “offers a timely occasion to uphold, affirm and reiterate our country’s lawful rights and entitlements.”

“Defending what is ours demands our solidarity as a people and a firm national resolve,” he said. “To every Filipino, rest assured that we will remain resolute in protecting our waters and safeguarding the future of our Bagong Pilipinas,” he said.
Pacific nations
The Philippines underscored its keen interest to work closely with Pacific nations on critical maritime issues, sea-level rise response and the promotion and adherence to UNCLOS.

The country reaffirmed its Pacific affinity and kinship while highlighting closer collaboration with fellow Pacific nations during the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders’ Meeting (55PIFLM) held in Koror, Palau from Aug. 30 to Sept. 4.
The Philippine delegation emphasized the mutual commitment to strong maritime governance in adherence to international law, particularly the UNCLOS.

Marcos designated Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim of the Department of Foreign Affairs as special envoy to the forum, which gathered the leaders of 18 Pacific nations – Australia, Cook Islands, Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Naoero, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu – as well as the PIF Secretariat.
Philippines, Canada meet
Defense officials of the Philippines and Canada met yesterday to explore ways to advance their bilateral defense cooperation.

Department of National Defense (DND) Undersecretary for Information Systems and Cybersecurity Fabian Pedregosa met with Senior Associate Deputy Minister of National Defense Kevin Brosseau on the sidelines of the Seoul Defense Dialogue.

Following the Senate concurrence on the Philippine-Canada Status of Visiting Forces Agreement this year, the two sides expressed their optimism for Canada’s participation in bilateral exercises, as well as multilateral engagements with other SOVFA partners like the United States, Japan and Australia. – Helen Flores, Pia Lee-Brago

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is seeking an immigration lookout bulletin order against Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste and six others linked to an alleged honey trap planned against Executive Secretary Ralph Recto.
Photos showed Leviste getting into an Uber in France, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said.
“That was on Aug. 6, after which he went to Switzerland. The latest information is that he is in France,” Matibag said.
Matibag will seek the Department of Justice’s issuance of an immigration alert to prevent Leviste and others from evading legal proceedings.
Qualified human trafficking charges were filed on Sept. 4 by the NBI against Leviste and others involved in an alleged scheme to frame Recto.
Leviste and his mother Sen. Loren Legarda left the country on Aug. 2.
Authorities can coordinate with Philippine embassies and the International Police Organization once arrest warrants are issued, Matibag said.
Arresting them would be a challenge if respondents abroad apply for asylum, he noted.
“I hope he comes home to face the case,” Matibag said.

articles.title: Remullas flying to France for Co
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla and his brother Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla are planning to fly separately to France in pursuit of those facing criminal cases in the Philippines.

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla and his brother Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla are planning to fly separately to France in pursuit of those facing criminal cases in the Philippines.

After the Sandiganbayan issued an arrest warrant for plunder against former congressman Zaldy Co, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) chief said yesterday he would fly to France to personally meet with officials of the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) at their headquarters in Lyon.

“We will file another request for a red notice against Zaldy Co. Coincidentally, I will also go to Lyon, France to follow up on his red notice from Interpol,” he said at a news briefing in Camp Crame.
The ombudsman earlier said he would also fly to France to talk to French authorities about prominent personalities accused of corruption who are believed to be hiding in the European country.
“I will work with the Interpol, he (DILG chief) will work with the diplomatic efforts to get Zaldy Co,” the ombudsman said.
A red notice seeks the location and arrest of a person wanted by a judicial jurisdiction or international tribunal.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division on Monday ordered the arrest of former House speaker Martin Romualdez, Co, Romualdez’s household staff Joselyn Serenio and money changer owner Felicito Guevarra after they were indicted for a P7.4-billion plunder charge.

The government earlier sought a red notice alert for Co after the anti-graft court’s Sixth Division issued an arrest warrant for graft and malversation of public funds over an allegedly anomalous road dike project in Oriental Mindoro worth P289.5 million.
As for Serenio and Guevarra, Remulla said manhunt operations are ongoing for their arrest.
Political will

The arrest of Romualdez over the flood control scandal should finally silence critics accusing President Marcos of being a weak leader, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said, urging the public to let the judicial process take its course.
Posting on X on Monday, Lacson said the arrest of the President’s cousin demonstrates the administration’s political will to exact accountability.

“With the arrest of his cousin, former speaker Romualdez, the President’s critics who have accused him of weak leadership and a lack of resolve in confronting the flood-control mess should now be silenced by his action,” he said.
The senator commended the Sandiganbayan for advancing the case.
“The ombudsman likewise deserves all the praise and support from the Filipino people,” Lacson continued.
“Let the trial proceed and let the evidence speak. Most importantly, the former speaker is now given his day in court,” he added.
During his tenure as Senate Blue Ribbon chair, Lacson had repeatedly invited Romualdez to attend the flood control hearings, but the former speaker failed to appear.

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon yesterday affirmed the administration’s adherence to judicial process, following Romualdez’s arrest, emphasizing that legal accountability must apply equally without special accommodations such as hospital arrest.

On questions regarding potential petitions from Romualdez’s camp seeking hospital arrest or alternative detention arrangements on health and comfort grounds, Dizon maintained that judicial processes must remain strictly neutral.

“My personal stance is that justice needs to be completely fair and equal,” Dizon said. “When ordinary citizens or DPWH engineers face criminal or administrative charges, they do not receive special detention accommodations or hospital privileges. We leave the final decision to the courts, but equal application of the law must prevail.”
Ang pleads not guilty

Meanwhile, USWAG Ilonggo Party-list Rep. Jojo Ang has entered a “not guilty” plea before the Sandiganbayan Second Division for two counts of graft for alleged conflict of interest in government infrastructure projects.
Ombudsman prosecutors have accused Ang of maintaining an unlawful financial interest in a construction firm that secured government contracts.
The court has set the pre-trial of the cases to Sept. 15 pending consolidation of Ang’s separate graft charges from the anti-graft court’s Fourth Division.
The ombudsman has filed a total of 14 counts of graft against Ang over his supposed beneficial ownership of Allencon Development Corp., where he owns 500 shares.

Ang is reportedly the nephew of the owners of International Builders Corp., the biggest contractor in Western Visayas Region. The firm was reportedly the contractor of two allegedly substandard flyover projects in Iloilo worth more than P1.7 billion.
He allegedly remained a co-owner of the family-run firm for nearly a year after taking office in 2022. – Neil Jayson Servallos, Rainier Allan Ronda, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Suspect held in Germany after spate of sabotage attacks on power grid
articles.summary: The suspect had reportedly claimed responsibility for attacks on electricity substations in letters.

blocks.text: A 48-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of carrying out a spate of sabotage attacks on Germany's electricity grid after spending several days on the run.
The suspect was carrying explosives when he was detained near the Weisweiler power plant in western Germany on Tuesday, police in Cologne said.
A tent in nearby undergrowth was also found to be rigged with further explosives, they added.

The suspect, named by German media as Daniel V, is believed to have written letters claiming responsibility for the attacks, which have taken place in Brandenburg and Saxony in the east as well North Rhine-Westphalia in the west.
Police said explosives found during the arrest were being examined by a bomb disposal expert, while officers were checking to see if any undiscovered devices had been set up in the surrounding area.
Prior to the suspect's arrest on Tuesday, police said they had found several launch devices on high-voltage lines near the Weisweiler plant on Monday afternoon, alongside "another confession letter".
A series of incidents across the grid in the last week have followed a similar pattern, with rockets used to shoot wires across high-voltage cables in order to cause short circuits.
The attacks have led to power-generating units at some plants being temporarily taken off the grid.

A statement from the Cologne Public Prosecutor's Office and Cologne Police on Tuesday did not provide further details on the suspect, or on the number and whereabouts of incidents he has been linked to.

German media have previously reported receiving two letters from the suspect claiming responsibility for the attacks. The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said the handwritten letters contained information that had not yet been made public.

The letters were apparently signed with the first name Daniel, while his surname was kept anonymous, in line with German privacy rules. The letters also gave a residential address in the town of Gevelsberg.

Cologne Police had previously said it was searching for a 48-year-old suspect from the town in connection with the sabotage of electrical substations in three German states. Investigators had also said explosives were found during a search of the suspect's apartment.
In Saxony alone, police found 21 devices near high-voltage power lines last Friday and Saturday.
Interior Minister Armin Schuster has admitted it could have led to a regional blackout, but he has warned against jumping to conclusions.
"The way this deed was committed makes this case unusual, as well as the manner of the confession," he said.

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Dredging of the NLEx section of the Tulaoc River is complete, and as of Sept. 8, NLEx Corp. reports there is no more pooling of rainwater on the expressway shoulder. The company…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Dredging of the NLEx section of the Tulaoc River is complete, and as of Sept. 8, NLEx Corp. reports there is no more pooling of rainwater on the expressway shoulder.

The company added that the work is continuing upstream from the Manila Bay outfall toward Tulaoc and the expressway, carried out with government and private sector partners. Deployment upstream was not possible during the flooding itself, when standing water blocked truck access.
Sheet piles installed along the alignment to keep water out of the NLEx system are being monitored through the rainfall now forecast.

Dredging is one part of the flood mitigation measures on the corridor. A mobile pumping unit is deployed at the kilometer 56 marker, with L-type flood barriers and modular mesh-and-liner units along the alignment and crews pre-positioned at Meycauayan, Paso de Blas, San Fernando and Balintawak.

Toll relief for journeys the expressway did not deliver—P113 for Class 1, P281 for Class 2 and P338 for Class 3—was credited to motorists’ RFID accounts the following day, with no claim form required.

“Our section of the river is dredged, and there is no water on the shoulder,” NLEx Corp. said. “The work is moving upstream from the bay, and we are watching the sheet piles perform through the next rainfall.” /cb

articles.title: DSWD gets lower budget for 4Ps, AICS in 2027 NEP
articles.summary: Two of the flagship programs of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) will get budget cuts under the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 11:28pm
Two of the flagship programs of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) will get budget cuts under the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).

According to a "24 Oras" report by Tina Panganiban-Perez, the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) was allocated P99.1 billion in 2027 to cover 3.5 million households. For 2026, DSWD received P112.9 billion for 4.4 million households.
For 2025, the poverty threshold—the minimum income required for a family to meet its basic food and non-food needs—was set at a national average of P14,634 per month, up from P13,873 in 2023.
This means a family whose monthly income falls below the threshold is considered poor.
On a daily basis, the poverty threshold is equivalent to a family income of about P487.
For a typical family of five, this translates to about P97 per person per day.
Poor and near-poor families, or those earning 10 percent higher than the poverty threshold, are among the beneficiaries of the 4Ps program.
But DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said near-poor families should include those earning 25 percent above the poverty threshold.

"We met with PSA (Philippine Statistics Authority) yesterday. It is high time to revisit the statistical definition of the near poor so that it is not only limited to 10% above the poverty threshold but up to 25% above the threshold because these are households with the same characteristic of poor but just above the poverty line," Gatchalian explained.
Meanwhile, the budget for the social pension of indigent senior citizens also suffered a slight cut, from P51.8 billion this year to P51.8 billion in the 2027 NEP.
Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS), which has P63.9 billion in 2026, got a drastic cut under the 2027 NEP at P33 billion.
Several lawmakers raised concern about the possibility of the AICS fund being used for politics.

"Iyong AICS naman, may proseso siyang pinagdaraanan. Anybody can refer, pero dadaan pa rin yan sa masusing pagsusuri at pag-aaral ng ating mga social worker. The vetting process is there. That's our safety net," he said.
The DSWD also sought additional budget for its Quick Response Fund (QRF) for calamities. From P3 billion in 2026, the QRF was allocated only P1 billion in 2027. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Netanyahu was warned of 7 October Hamas attacks, book claims
articles.summary:
Israeli PM says allegation that UAE president alerted him more than a week before major offensive is ‘absolute lie’

Benjamin Netanyahu was personally alerted by the president of the United…

blocks.text: Benjamin Netanyahu was personally alerted by the president of the United Arab Emirates that Hamas was planning a large-scale offensive against Israel a week before its 7 October 2023 attack, but did not act on the warning, according to a book by Haaretz reporters.

The claim, which comes amid a crucial election campaign, prompted Israeli opposition leaders to describe the prime minister as “unfit” for office, even as Netanyahu denounced the report as an “absolute lie” and denied he spoke to the Emirati leader at that time.

Haaretz said the Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar, later killed by Israel, had warned a former Palestinian official that the militants were preparing “a terrifying operation” which he described as an “earthquake”.
According to the report, the UAE president, Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, spoke to Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack, and told him Hamas was planning a major operation.
The allegations, published in Haaretz on Tuesday, pile more pressure on the Israeli prime minister who has already faced heavy criticism for his handling of events before the 7 October attacks.

Hamas militants killed more than 1,200 people and took another 251 people hostage during the offensive. Hundreds of Israelis, mostly soldiers, have been killed in continued fighting from consequent wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Israel’s retaliatory offensive has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 73,000 Palestinians.
The claims are contained in the book Hostages: 843 Days of Abandonment, which, its authors say, is based on dozens of sources in Israel and worldwide, including very senior officials.

According to Haaretz, bin Zayed communicated frequently with senior Israeli leaders, including Netanyahu and the Israeli president Isaac Herzog, with a UAE diplomat delivering a secure phone to the Israeli prime minister for the conversations.

A week and a half before 7 October, the reporters say, bin Zayed called Netanyahu from the presidential palace in Abu Dhabi and, in a 45-minute call, warned that Sinwar was planning a major operation which the Emirati leader was concerned could destabilise the region.
To bin Zayed’s surprise, Netanyahu reacted calmly to the news, the report said.
In a joint statement on Tuesday, several Israeli opposition party leaders declared their intention to find out what Netanyahu knew and when, and what actions he took, if any.
“Why did he not inform the security establishment, and why did he not act to protect Israeli citizens?” the statement demanded.

Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander who has emerged as Netanyahu’s main rival in the October elections, accused the long-serving prime minister of evading responsibility for security lapses and resorting to “pathetic” excuses, such as saying he was not woken up soon enough on the morning of the attack.
“Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for 7 October and ignored them all. He is unfit,” Eisenkot wrote on X.

Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in the elections, said Netanyahu “bears personal and direct responsibility” for the deaths on 7 October, the deadliest attack in Israeli history. “Netanyahu cannot continue to serve in his position for even one more minute,” Bennett said.
The leader of the centre-left Democrats party, Yair Golan, accused Netanyahu of “endangering Israel”.
“The stories about ‘no one woke me up’ are over. You knew, you ignored, you failed, you are to blame,” he said, in a video posted on social media.
Many Israelis have demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into the security lapses that failed to prevent Hamas’s attack.

Opposition parties say establishing such a commission, whose members would be appointed by the supreme court, would be their first priority if elected. Netanyahu’s government has rejected the proposal.

articles.title: Quebec 'will use every tool available' to cope with trade war, Fréchette says
articles.summary: Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette warned of difficult times ahead and called on Quebecers and municipalities to pivot away from American businesses and support the local economy, in a news…

image.caption: Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette held a news conference Tuesday morning to touch on the measures her government announced to help the province cope with counter-tariffs imposed by Canada on certain American products that went into effect just after midnight. (Dany Pilote/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal

Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette warned of difficult times ahead and called on Quebecers and municipalities to pivot away from American businesses and support the local economy, in a news conference Tuesday morning.
Fréchette estimates the value of public tender measure to help businesses at $1.5B

"Quebec will not back down in the face of Trump," she said, describing the U.S. president as a bully. "In fact, we will use every tool available to the state to buy more Quebec-made products in order to protect our jobs, protect our economy and protect our workers."

Fréchette, who is in the midst of a provincial election, announced new measures Monday evening to help the province cope with Canada's counter-tariffs on several American products. They went into effect just after midnight.
The measures include giving Quebec-based companies an advantage in public tenders as well as steps to help them find new markets across Canada.
On Tuesday, she said the measures affect $1.5 billion in contracts over the next four months, adding that American businesses generally represent under 10 per cent of public contract bidders.
When asked if she feared further retaliation from President Donald Trump, she said that at this point she wouldn't be surprised if there was, given how the last year has unfolded.
"We will still go forward because we need to strengthen our economy and to be united. And we are inviting everyone who can be part of that movement to answer the movement," she said.

items: U.S., Canada trade reps expected to speak today, sources say, as Ottawa's counter-tariffs take effect

blocks.text: Tuesday morning, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the U.S. will consider imposing retaliatory tariffs on Canadian goods as early as today.
Quebec 'will not back down in the face of Trump,' premier says
Measuring the impact on Quebec
Fréchette said Canada's counter-tariffs are expected to impact 8.8 per cent of the country's imports, including five per cent of Quebec's imports.
She said the impact on Quebec's job market is still to be determined, adding that August alone saw 18,000 layoffs across the province.
"So, for sure that's not dissociated from the tariff war," she said in French on Tuesday.

items: Carney warns of tough times ahead in video message as retaliatory tariffs kick in

blocks.text: The premier also said federal rebates should effectively neutralize the counter-tariff burden on Canadian businesses. She called on the federal government to make sure those reimbursement processes are efficient, fast and easy to navigate.
She said there isn't a meeting of the premiers planned in the coming days as far as she knows.
Fréchette stepped away from the campaign trail Monday to convene her cabinet and discuss Quebec's strategy in the face of Canada's retaliatory tariffs just before they came into force.

items: Quebec moves to protect supply chains, expand relief to more businesses as trade war intensifies

blocks.text: In the lead-up to that meeting, the Coalition Avenir Québec leader was accused by rival parties of using the tariff war to gain traction among voters. She addressed those claims on Tuesday.
"This is real life, and we need to face it, and we need to adjust our approach," she said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Cassandra Yanez-Leyton is a journalist for CBC News based in Montreal. You can email her story ideas at cassandra.yanez-leyton@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Sudan's healthcare system on brink of collapse after cuts, medical charity warns
articles.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières is urging world leaders to increase funding to help the millions who need aid.

blocks.text: Sudan's fragile health system is on the brink of collapse as global funding cuts have led to the closure of healthcare facilities across the country, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned.
Dozens of organisations were unable to find alternative funding after the US - the largest donor to Sudan - closed USAID, its body for delivering foreign aid, last year, the medical charity said.
MSF urged world leaders gathering at the UN General Assembly in New York to take action.

The war that erupted in April 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, with more than 33 million people needing medical assistance.
MSF said while the US was still the largest donor to Sudan, existing grants to many USAID-funded organisations ran out in June - as European governments were also reducing international assistance.
According to the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), international aid fell globally by 21.3% in 2025 compared to the previous year.
"War is driving Sudan's needs; funding cuts are shrinking the response," said Muhammad Ibrahim, the head of charity in Sudan.

"MSF's work in Sudan is privately funded. But when funding disappears from other health services, clinics close, patients have fewer places to go, and pressure shifts to the facilities that remain, including ours."
This has meant that patients often have to make dangerous and long trips to get treatment.

"After a longer and more expensive journey, patients often arrive in a much more serious condition, and the hospital may already be full," explained Sebastián Traficante, MSF's emergency co-ordinator in the western region of Darfur, which has experienced much of the fighting over the last three years.
Between January and April 2026, MSF saw admissions jump by 22.5% in facilities it supports in central Darfur, when compared to the same time last year.
In May alone, 45 healthcare centres in the area had stopped receiving funding, it said.
According to MSF, the closure of frontline services was putting other hospitals under severe strain - as they were losing their capacity to function and medicines were disappearing.

It gave Gedaref state's Tanedba camp, where 18,400 people who have fled their homes live, as an example. Its maternity and surgical wards have closed down after a humanitarian organisation left in June.
As a result, MSF is now running an emergency room there, but pregnant women who need surgery to deliver a baby, have to travel three hours to the nearest city.
In the Um Rakuba camp - also in Gedaref - the number of aid agencies working there has dropped from 35 in 2021, to less than 10.
According to the charity, the camp currently hosts around 17,000 people, most of whom are women and children.
"If support does not increase, more patients will face longer journeys, fewer treatment options and greater risk of arriving too late for care," MSF's UK humanitarian representative Liz Harding said.
At the same time as the health system was struggling with funding, attacks on healthcare workers were continuing, MSF said.
In 2025, Sudan saw 1,620 people killed in attacks on medical facilities - which the charity said accounted for 82% of all global deaths from attacks on healthcare worldwide.
According to the UN, more than 19.5 million people are also experiencing "crisis levels" of food insecurity and more than five million are facing "emergency levels of hunger".
The fighting shows no sign of easing - despite the expected arrival of international diplomats in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, for consultations aimed at ending the civil war.

Reports from North Kordofan state on Tuesday say at least 11 people have been killed in a drone attack on the army-controlled town of Umm Ruwaba. According to medical sources, the projectile struck a crowded courtyard in a court complex.

articles.title: In West Bank, date farmers weigh impact of UK sanctions on Israeli settlers
articles.summary: Palestinians strongly back a ban on settlement goods, but Israel's government says it is a "big mistake".

blocks.text: Dates are among the agricultural products commonly exported from Israeli settlements in the West Bank
ByYolande Knell
Middle East correspondent
Juicy brown and ripening yellow dates dangle down from the branches of each palm tree at Israeli settler farms in the Jordan Valley, in the occupied West Bank.
This year, as Israeli growers get ready for a good harvest, they are also preparing for the impact of new Western sanctions against settlements, which are illegal under international law.

The UK government has announced an import ban on settlement goods and said it planned to take action against companies and individuals who provide services for settlement expansion, as part of what it calls a "comprehensive reset" of policy towards Israel following similar moves by several other European countries.

Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden have also confirmed their intention to introduce national restrictions, or support European restrictions, on trade in goods with settlements.
Palestinians strongly back such a move, but Israel's president says it is a "grave miscalculation".
Israeli date farmer Avigdor Arbel, from the settlement of Mesua, calls such boycotts "really disgusting".
Arbel sells his produce mostly to Europe but also to the US and now, India. However, he says the sector is ready for any new UK ban on settler goods.

"As soon as we have a situation of pressure and boycotts, we always break out and look for other markets," he tells me. "So, I believe that if we get to a situation in which there's no place to sell my fruits in Europe, we'll find other markets."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Settler farmer Avigdor Arbel does not believe Israel will ever give up the Jordan Valley

blocks.text: Settler farmer Avigdor Arbel does not believe Israel will ever give up the Jordan Valley

West Bank settlements have expanded rapidly under the current Israeli government, whose ministers say they want "to bury the idea" of an independent Palestinian state - part of the long-standing international formula for peace in the region known as the two-state solution.
At the same time, settler violence against Palestinians has surged to what the UN says is "an all-time high".

With new settler outposts - which are also illegal under Israeli law - now dotting the barren hilltops of the Jordan Valley, there have been repeated attacks on local Palestinians, particularly Bedouin and herding communities.

In January, the last of some 600 villagers fled their homes in Ras Ein al-Ouja after intense harassment by hardline settlers, often backed by Israeli security forces. It was the largest single displacement of a Palestinian community in the past three years.
Further north, in March, Israeli settlers brutally beat and sexually assaulted a Palestinian shepherd during a night raid on Khirbet Humsa.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Parliament on Tuesday that a set of facts on the ground had been created "to make the two-state solution unviable," while "settler terrorism is rampant".

Quoting a former Israeli minister of health and retired brigadier general, Ephraim Sneh, he said the UK government "agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank perpetrated by settler terrorists", to which the Israeli government had "turned a blind eye" or actually supported.
In a significant change of UK policy, he said the government now agreed with the 2024 International Court of Justice advisory opinion that Israel's continued occupation "is unlawful".
As a consequence, Miliband said this should be reflected "in the economic relationships we choose to have with the occupied territories".
"I do not believe that the British people want us supporting the occupation by accepting products from settlements in our shops and supermarkets."

blocks.caption: Image caption, The Jordan Valley is a fertile strip of land that comprises nearly 30% of the West Bank

blocks.text: The Jordan Valley is a fertile strip of land that comprises nearly 30% of the West Bank
Medjool dates are the main export crop from both Israeli settler farms and Palestinian farms in the Jordan Valley.

"These are rubbish," says Palestinian farmer Abdul Halim Abu Omar, dramatically reaching up and throwing away a handful of shrivelled, yellow dates from a tree in the grove where he works in al-Ouja, north of Jericho.

Around half of the date palms here have no fruit at all. "It's because we lack water," Abu Omar says. His is an extreme case: this year, the trees he cares for have received less than a third of the water they need to thrive.
Access to water has long been a pressing issue in the West Bank.
Interim peace agreements from the 1990s have left a water disparity between Israelis and Palestinians, and Israeli authorities typically prioritise water for settlers over Palestinians' needs.
Recently, in rural areas of the Jordan Valley, almost all of which is under Israeli security and civilian control, extremist settlers have also taken over several freshwater springs.
The Israeli Civil Administration told the BBC that it keeps "continuous contact" with the Palestinian Water Authority and assists in carrying out repairs to water infrastructure.

This harvest time, Abu Omar has few dates that are fit to show local Palestinian exporter Momen Sinokrot. His firm, Palestine Gardens, works with 55 date growers in the Jordan Valley to sell to several European countries, including the UK.
Sinokrot believes that if more states ban settlement trade this could curb settlement growth.
"Settlers are very active in the Jordan Valley... and they are not obeying any laws or rules or anything even from the Israeli army itself," he says.
"They are going to the fields of the growers, they are stealing from them, and they are controlling more and more land."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Palestinian farmer Abdul Halim says half his date farms have no fruit because of a water shortage

blocks.text: Palestinian farmer Abdul Halim says half his date farms have no fruit because of a water shortage

Israeli-state support for settlements, as well as their relatively easy access to global markets, means that Palestinian farmers struggle to compete. Palestinian businesses face greater restrictions and costs to export across Israeli-controlled borders.

Palestinians want the wide swathe of fertile land in the Jordan Valley - along the West Bank's border with Jordan - as part of their own hoped-for future state, along with the rest of the West Bank and Gaza, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
However, Avigdor Arbel, the settler date farmer, does not believe that his country will ever give up the Jordan Valley. He has lived there since the 1970s.

Within years of Israel's capture of the West Bank from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East War, the Israeli government began encouraging its citizens to move to this area to counter what it saw as the security risk along the border.
More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the West Bank, not including Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem, alongside three million Palestinians.
There are 340 settler outposts in the Palestinian territory along with 146 settlements, formally recognised by the Israeli government, according to the Israeli anti-settlement group Peace Now.
Current UK and EU laws require labels for settlement goods. Agricultural produce commonly exported includes mangoes, avocados, herbs and grapes.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Israeli settlers diverted a Palestinian village's water to fill a pool in the Jordan Valley this summer

blocks.text: Israeli settlers diverted a Palestinian village's water to fill a pool in the Jordan Valley this summer
There have been questions raised about how a ban on settlement goods would be enforced.

A recent report by the legal advocacy group Global Echo found that some settlement fruits and vegetables sold in Europe were inaccurately identified as coming from Israel - or mingled with produce from inside Israel's internationally-recognised borders.

However, the report's author, Jessica Stober, suggests that a UK ban on settler goods would greatly increase the financial costs associated with any such fraudulent practices. Instead of a seller being fined for misrepresenting their goods, the shipment would be returned.
"A ban is more self-enforcing because you have involved the private sector and it becomes commercially unviable for them to deal in settlement goods," Stober says.

"I would also say that a whole new set of measures become available to the UK government under a sanctions regime, under a ban, including civil and criminal penalties that make compliance much more likely."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Palestinian exporter Momen Sinokrot believes sanctions could help curb settlement growth

blocks.text: Palestinian exporter Momen Sinokrot believes sanctions could help curb settlement growth
Speaking just before the UK move was announced, Israeli President Isaac Herzog said it would amount to "gross interference" in Israel's upcoming elections, due in late October.
"I believe it will prove to be a grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history," he warned.
Israel's government is threatening retaliation for any UK ban on settlement goods.

"If Britain acts against the State of Israel, the State of Israel will act against Britain," the Israeli Foreign Secretary, Gideon Saar, told an Israeli podcast last week. When I approached him at a diplomatic event on Monday to ask for more details about which steps could be taken, he declined to answer.
Israel recently expelled two Dutch diplomats from a US-led centre in charge of co-ordinating the shaky Gaza ceasefire, after the Netherlands banned trade from settlements.
Other European countries that have already imposed a ban on settlement goods or trade restrictions - arguing it is a legal obligation - include Ireland, Spain and Belgium.
Now, the new action by the UK looks set to put a new, heavy strain on its relations with Israel.

articles.title: Flushing the toilet can release a ‘plume’ of breathable pathogens – and closing the lid won’t stop their escape
articles.summary:
New research shows turbulent flushes create toilet-generated aerosols that can transmit legionella, influenza and norovirus

  • Get our

blocks.text: Flushing toilets release particles into the “breathing zone” of adults and can remain suspended in the air for at least 20 seconds, a new study has found.
And closing the lid might not be enough to avoid a “plume” of potential pathogens.
Meanwhile, previous research has shown public toilets are an inescapable hotbed of microbes.
Flinders University researchers reviewed 22 studies of toilet-generated aerosols, publishing the results in the Science of the Total Environment journal.
They found microbes from the water used for flushing or from contamination of the bowl ended up as aerosols, with more “turbulent” flushing releasing more particles.

That included bioaerosols – aerosols that contain biological material and can transmit pathogens including legionella, influenza and norovirus. There are differing reports about whether Covid spreads through toilet aerosols.

The researchers found higher levels of aerosols in the water and higher levels of turbulence during the flush increased the volume of particles suspended in the air, but the effects of bathroom ventilation and whether the lid was up or down were unclear.
Despite that, lead author and PhD student Lira Adiyani said she would still recommend putting the lid down after using the toilet.
“Toilet flushing creates turbulence that can release aerosols into the surrounding air,” she said.
“Some studies detected these aerosols at adult breathing height, indicating a potential pathway for inhalation exposure.
“The more microbes present in the toilet, the more bioaerosols may be released. Therefore, larger flush volumes generally produce more aerosols.”
Adiyani said “based on the available evidence” she would still recommend closing the lid as a precautionary measure, “while recognising that it does not completely prevent aerosols from escaping”.

In the report, the researchers wrote that the effects of indoor aerosols had been “understudied” despite the risk of infection. This had “important implications for risk assessment, building design, and infection control in an era of water security pressures and emerging infectious diseases”, they wrote.
“Indoor aerosols influence air quality and human health as their small size allows them to penetrate deep into the respiratory tract when inhaled, providing a direct exposure pathway.”
Co-author, environmental health professor Harriet Whiley, said people didn’t have to be worried in their own homes, unless someone in the house was immunocompromised.
She said the team was working on “protecting the most vulnerable through good design” in places such as hospitals and aged care environments.
after newsletter promotion

They are increasingly concerned about “opportunistic pathogens” that can be present in water, particularly recycled or rainwater. “They don’t affect healthy people,” she said. “But if you’re immunocompromised you can get very sick, and it can be fatal.”
So it’s about getting “an effective flush with less volume and less turbulence”, she said.
Dr Lotti Tajouri, an associate professor in molecular genetics at Bond and Murdoch universities wasn’t involved in the research but warned bathroom dangers go well beyond the toilet.
His own research is particularly focused on public toilets and mobile phone use in toilets.
“As soon as you enter a toilet, consider everything contaminated,” he said.
The door will have microbes on it, as will the floor – so you should never put anything on it, he said. Then you might touch the lid, after which you flush with the lid up or down.
If it’s up, you get the “plume” effect, an “explosion or aerosols … you are literally sprayed [with]”.

Flushing with the lid down might limit your exposure to the plume, but depending on the cleanliness of the toilet, previous users have left microorganisms on every surface anyway. “The roof, the walls, the floor,” he said.

Then, you touch the toilet door again, before (hopefully) washing your hands. But you will probably touch the taps again, blow microorganisms around with the hairdryer, touch the exit door and then touch your phone.

“Studies show between 50% and 80% of people use mobile phones in the toilet. For younger generations it’s almost 100%,” he said. “They will contaminate their phones and fingers with fecal microorganisms – salmonella, campylobacter, all sorts of bacteria and viruses.
“The less contact you have, the better it is.”

articles.title: Senate Committee of the Whole to tackle Pax Silica issue
articles.summary: The Senate is set to take up the issue of the Pax Silica initiative through the Committee of the Whole, which will assemble the entire Upper Chamber into a panel for one specific issue.

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 10:56pm
The Senate is set to take up the issue of the Pax Silica initiative through the Committee of the Whole, which will assemble the entire Upper Chamber into a panel for one specific issue.
Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri made the motion to refer the Pax Silica to the Committee of the Whole during a Senate session on Tuesday.

“So that all members can be represented. All Committee Chairs can be represented but you’re the presiding officer, Mister President,” Zubiri said, addressing Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian.

“And I think it would be best to show that we are serious either in support or we're concerned about Pax Silica because it's really a very, very important measure that needs to be given undue attention and the discussions will not be limited only to the environment and economic affairs,” he added.

The Vice Chairs of the Committee of the Whole would be the current chairs of the Committee on Environment, Committee on Cultural Communities and Muslim Affairs, Committee on Economic Affairs, Committee on Trade, Commerce and Entrepreneurship.
Explainer: Pax Silica– why are people worried?
Respectively, these would be senators Raffy Tulfo, Robin Padilla, Risa Hontiveros, and Bam Aquino. Zubiri himself would also be a Vice Chair as the Chair of the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Gatchalian said that the matter was urgent since the project was already ongoing.
“I will heed to your suggestion. With that motion, is there any objection? Hearing none, the motion of the Majority Leader to create the Paxilica Committee of the Whole is approved,” Gatchalian said.
Previous occasions when the Senate assembled the Committee of the Whole include the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, as well as agricultural smuggling in 2022.

The Pax Silica initiative in the New Clark City in Tarlac has generated concerns on its possible impact on the environment and energy security. Locals in the area also fear displacement and homelessness should the project push through. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: British family speaks out over nine-year ordeal after husband is abducted by Saudi Arabia
articles.summary:
Mira Lozi says quiet diplomacy has failed to free Rami Naimi who was first seized in Dubai in 2017

A British woman has spoken out for the first time about the alleged abduction, torture and…

blocks.text: A British woman has spoken out for the first time about the alleged abduction, torture and coercion of her husband at the hands of Saudi authorities, after nine years of “failed” quiet diplomacy.
The businessman Rami Naimi was first abducted in Dubai in 2017 on his return from a trip to Australia with his father. After being tortured, he was released the following year.

The father of three, who is the son of Ali Al-Naimi, a former Saudi oil minister and head of the state oil company Aramco, was detained again in 2022 and held for two years. Last year he was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment after a secret trial.

He was initially detained alongside 400 of the kingdom’s most powerful people in an infamous round-up at the the Ritz-Carlton hotel in Riyadh, which became the biggest and most contentious purge in the modern kingdom’s history.

Speaking out for the first time after years of what they described as a failed diplomatic process, his family has alleged abduction, disappearance, torture and coercion at the hands of Saudi authorities.
Naimi now faces a second trial for allegedly following certain accounts on X critical of Saudi Arabia and for attempting to leave the country without permission – both of which he denies.
“The first thing I wanted to do was speak out, but I was told no,” said his wife Mira Lozi, speaking alongside her son at a campaign launch to bring Naimi home in London on Tuesday.
Lozi, currently fighting cancer, fought back tears as she said she had been encouraged to keep silent since 2017 to help secure his release.

“For nine years my children and I have lived through a nightmare,” she said. “Saying the truth today is like a liberation, enough is enough and we’re just hoping that we can end this nightmare and all the governments will be able to help us.”

blocks.caption: Mira Lozi with her husband, Rami Naimi. Photograph: Bring Rami Home Campaign/PA

blocks.text: Naimi left Saudi Arabia aged 13 and travelled for years between the UK, US and Middle East as a businessman. His family claim he was abducted in Dubai in 2017 returning home from a book tour trip from Australia with his father.

They say he was blindfolded and forcibly taken by car to Abu Dhabi and then by private jet to Saudi Arabia. He was surprised to find himself with the others who had been rounded up, his family said, as he is not a journalist, activist or politician.

His abduction in 2017 came as the kingdom’s elite were detained at a five-star hotel in Riyadh during a purge in which princes, tycoons and ministers were stripped of their fortunes. Accounts later surfaced detailing torture and coercion, and the event preceded the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, whose assassination at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in 2018 sparked revulsion around the world.

Naimi was held at the hotel and tortured, electrocuted, waterboarded and psychologically abused for three months, his family said. He was told, falsely, that his father was being tortured next door. He was released in January 2018 after signing a “settlement agreement”.

He was subsequently forced to sign a document pledging to surrender 5bn Saudi riyals, later “discounted” to 1bn riyals (£200m) – which the family says neither he or they possess. Naimi was placed under electronic surveillance and banned from leaving the kingdom.

His family said he was disappeared again for nearly two years in 2022, and subjected to further torture, and emotional and psychological abuse. They said they had no idea if he was alive or dead, and learned only through the help of his legal team and diplomats that he was being held in Saudi’s notorious Al Ha’ir prison.

It was after his release in March 2025, with an electronic tag and subject to a travel ban, that he learned of charges against him claiming he had “exploited” his father’s official influence. Naimi faced allegations he acted as an agent for a US company in Saudi Arabia and helped Aramco to secure a contract to provide technology to prevent diesel smuggling.

After seven years without charges, Naimi, an EU citizen, was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment following a secret trial. Now he is unable to leave Saudi Arabia and his communications with his family remain monitored. He has no idea, the family said, of their decision to go public with his case.
“Until today we have no idea why Rami was targeted,” said Lozi, who is too frightened to return to Saudi Arabia or travel to the United Arab Emirates.
“It really is something out of a movie. It’s shocking and we just want to end this nightmare,” said his 21-year-old son, Ali, who was 12 when his father was abducted.

In recent years the UK’s relationship with Saudi Arabia has come under scrutiny over the flow of arms between the two countries, Riyadh’s use of public executions and targeting of exiled activists and dissidents.
“Any family making a decision like this needs to be supported by the government,” said human rights lawyer Caoilfhionn Gallagher KC, who is leading the case.

As the family hopes to meet the new prime minister and foreign secretary, Gallagher said the recent appointment of a special envoy for Britons detained overseas does not go as far as campaigners, experts and parliamentarians had called for.
Gallagher described it as: “Tea and sympathy for a very limited group of people.”

Last month the Guardian reported that X had become the latest US social media company to block the accounts of Saudi dissidents so they are no longer visible inside the kingdom, following orders from Saudi authorities.
The UK Foreign Office declined to comment. The Saudi embassy in London has been approached for comment.
